figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: translational mechanics retold in angular language - mass, force, momentum get rotational twins
figures.read: every result is an analogue pair, a parallel-axis shift, or a no-slip constraint

figures.title: Two axis theorems: shift it or split it
figures.why: almost every inertia calculation is one of two moves
figures.data: parallel I = I_cm + Md²; perpendicular I_z = I_x + I_y
figures.read: parallel axis pushes outward by Md²; perpendicular splits flat-body inertia

figures.title: Torque: force times the lever arm
figures.why: the same force turns harder from farther out
figures.data: τ = rF sinθ moment arm; τ = Iα
figures.read: torque cares about the perpendicular distance to the line of action

figures.title: Angular momentum: constant when torque-free - even as KE changes
figures.why: L is frozen while kinetic energy rises, paid for by internal work
figures.data: L = Iω constant; I halves → ω doubles, K doubles
figures.read: conservation protects the product Iω, not the energy

figures.title: Rolling without slipping: two energies, one race
figures.why: the whole rolling toolkit in one figure
figures.data: v_cm = ωR; K = ½Mv² + ½Iω²; a = g sinθ / (1+I/MR²)
figures.read: rotation eats a share of energy set by I/MR²; smallest share wins

figures.title: Triage - route by the keyword
figures.why: the keyword names the route before any number is touched
figures.read: inertia wants axis theorems, rolling wants no-slip, torque-free words want conservation

drawings.title: The velocity field of a spinning disc
drawings.show: a disc rotating about its centre. At three points (centre, rim, and a point at $r/2$): velocity arrows drawn tangent to the circle. The centre has $v=0$. The rim has $v=R\omega$. The intermediate point has $v=(r/2)\omega$. The instantaneous axis through the centre shown as a dot.
drawings.search: "velocity field spinning disc instantaneous axis diagram"

drawings.title: Moment of inertia of six standard bodies
drawings.show: a rod, ring, disc, solid sphere, hollow sphere, and cylinder, each with the axis marked and the $I$ value labelled. The distance from axis to farthest mass element shown.
drawings.search: "moment of inertia standard bodies rod ring disc sphere cylinder table"

drawings.title: The parallel-axis theorem geometry
drawings.show: a disc with the COM axis (through the centre) and a parallel axis through the rim. The distance $d=R$ shown. $I_{\text{rim}}=I_{\text{cm}}+MR^2=MR^2/2+MR^2=3MR^2/2$.
drawings.search: "parallel axis theorem disc rim tangent geometry diagram"

drawings.title: Torque about a point with the moment arm
drawings.show: a force $\mathbf{F}$ applied at point $P$ on a body pivoted at $O$. The moment arm $d=r\sin\theta$ drawn as the perpendicular distance from $O$ to the line of action of $\mathbf{F}$. $\tau=Fd$ annotated.
drawings.search: "torque moment arm perpendicular distance force pivot diagram"

drawings.title: The rolling wheel's velocity field with the contact point at rest
drawings.show: a wheel rolling to the right at speed $v$. At the contact point: $v_{\text{contact}}=v-\omega R=0$ (no-slip condition). At the top: $v_{\text{top}}=v+\omega R=2v$. At the centre: $v_{\text{cm}}=v$. The velocity field shown as arrows of varying length around the wheel.
drawings.search: "rolling wheel velocity field contact point rest top 2v diagram"

drawings.title: The spinning skater: angular momentum conservation
drawings.show: a skater spinning with arms out ($I_1$ large, $\omega_1$ small) and arms in ($I_2$ small, $\omega_2$ large). $L=I_1\omega_1=I_2\omega_2$ annotated. The KE increases: $\frac{1}{2}I_2\omega_2^2>\frac{1}{2}I_1\omega_1^2$ — the extra energy comes from the work the skater does pulling her arms in.
drawings.search: "spinning skater angular momentum conservation arms in out kinetic energy"

drawings.title: The rolling race: five bodies at the same time
drawings.show: an incline with five bodies (solid sphere, solid cylinder, hollow sphere, hollow cylinder, sliding block) at the same time after release. The solid sphere is furthest ahead; the sliding block (no rotation) is even further. The $I/(MR^2)$ values annotated.
drawings.search: "rolling race incline solid sphere cylinder hollow sphere order diagram"

drawings.title: The slipping-to-rolling phase diagram
drawings.show: a graph of $v$ and $\omega R$ vs $t$. Initially $v>v_0$ and $\omega R=0$ (a ball thrown with no spin). $v$ decreases (friction opposes motion), $\omega R$ increases (friction creates torque). They meet at $t^*$ when $v=\omega R$ — rolling begins. After $t^*$: $v=\omega R$ (constant, no friction needed).
drawings.search: "slipping to rolling phase diagram v and omega R versus time"

drawings.title: A rod struck by a bullet
drawings.show: a rod hinged at one end, initially at rest. A bullet approaches at speed $v_0$ and embeds at distance $d$ from the hinge. The angular momentum about the hinge: $L_{\text{before}}=mv_0 d$. After: $L_{\text{after}}=(I_{\text{rod}}+md^2)\omega$.
drawings.search: "bullet hitting hinged rod angular momentum conservation diagram"

drawings.title: The ladder problem's force diagram with the incipient-tip normal force
drawings.show: a ladder leaning against a wall at angle $\theta$. Forces: weight $mg$ at the COM, normal force from the wall $N_w$ (horizontal), normal force from the ground $N_g$ (vertical), friction from the ground $f$ (horizontal). At the tipping point: $N_w$ acts at the top, $N_g$ acts at the bottom edge (not the centre of the base).
drawings.search: "ladder against wall force diagram tipping point normal force position"

drawings.title: A gyroscope with L, torque and the precession cone
drawings.show: a spinning top tilted at angle $\theta$ from the vertical. $\mathbf{L}$ along the spin axis. $\boldsymbol{\tau}=\mathbf{r}_{\text{cm}}\times M\mathbf{g}$ perpendicular to $\mathbf{L}$ (horizontal). $d\mathbf{L}=\boldsymbol{\tau}\,dt$ causes $\mathbf{L}$ to precess around the vertical. The precession cone drawn.
drawings.search: "gyroscope precession angular momentum torque cone diagram"

drawings.title: The collision-then-roll transition: bullet embeds in rod
drawings.show: a uniform rod of length $L$ hanging vertically from a frictionless hinge at the top. A bullet of mass $m$ approaches horizontally at speed $v$ and embeds at distance $d$ from the hinge. Three phases: (1) bullet approaches; (2) bullet embeds — angular momentum conserved about hinge; (3) rod swings up — energy conserved from post-collision KE to PE at maximum angle $\theta_{\max}$.
drawings.search: "bullet embeds in rod angular momentum conservation hinge rod swing diagram"
